thesis.problem: Cat owners need a playful way to remember and record recurring grooming and hygiene care.
thesis.target_user: Cat owners who actively care for and bond with their cats.
thesis.product_hypothesis: A whimsical grooming companion with a personalized digital cat can turn routine care into an engaging ritual while keeping a cloud record of grooming.
thesis.differentiation: Combines practical grooming tracking with playful virtual-pet progression instead of behaving like a conventional pet-health tracker.
thesis.product_direction: C: real-world grooming check-ins drive growth of a personalized digital cat
thesis.core_loop: Appropriate real care -> check-in -> gentle digital-cat progression -> care history/reminders

evidence.finding: Hygiene care tracking and reminders already exist
Pet-care reminders and to-dos already exist
Do not incentivize unnecessary ear cleaning or stressful grooming

risks: Grooming tasks may be too infrequent to create a strong retention loop.
The playful digital-cat layer may delight users without improving recurring care behavior.

validation.riskiest_assumption: Cat owners have enough recurring grooming pain or forgetfulness to return to a dedicated grooming app.
validation.cheapest_next_validation: Interview 5–8 cat owners about recent care tasks and missed care; compare simple tracker vs digital-cat progression prototype; invite to 2-week trial.
validation.positive_signal: Target users report recurring missed grooming or tracking friction and express intent to use the concept repeatedly.
validation.negative_signal: Most target users already manage grooming easily and see the experience as novelty-only.
validation.proposed_positive_threshold: At least 4/8 report concrete recent tracking friction and 4/8 opt into prototype trial (proposed)
validation.proposed_negative_threshold: Fewer than 2/8 report friction or fewer than 2/8 opt into trial (proposed)

decision.strongest_reason: The problem, audience, and differentiated playful product concept are coherent enough to explore.
decision.biggest_uncertainty: Whether recurring grooming creates enough real user need and frequency for retention.
decision.next_action: Conduct 5–8 problem interviews and prototype preference test; preserve EXPLORE and owner BUILD gate.
